market_context.summary: The Fed is hiking and the long end is repricing term premium, and that one fact governs most of this book. The 2026-09-16 FOMC raised the target range 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on a 12-0 vote — the first increase since July 2023 — with 16 of 18 participants projecting another; Kalshi last-traded 67c for a 25bp hike at the 2026-10-28 meeting this morning and 1c for a cut. The US 10-year is 5.18% (prev 5.11) against an effective funds rate of 3.88%, and 10s2s has steepened to +0.36 from +0.31 driven by the long end rather than by cuts — a term-premium steepener, not an easing one. The tape is coherent with that: leadership is tech (XLK -1.24% off its 90-day high), healthcare (XLV -3.34%) and energy (USO +44.8% off its low), while every rate-sensitive and consumer-facing group sits on its lows — XLP +0.90% off its 90-day low, XLRE +0.56%, IYR +0.58%, TLT +0.62% off a 250-day low, XLU +0.98%, with XLI, XLY, XLB, KRE, XRT and ITB all below both moving averages. KRE at -8.68% off its high says banks are not being paid for this steepener either. Crypto is selling with it: BTC 82,632 (-2.66% 24h), ETH 2,640 (-2.74%), SOL 117.70 (-5.36%). All equity and ETF prices here are the 2026-09-25 close, which is the freshest honest price at 6am ET on a Monday — a closed market, not stale data.

THREE IDEAS ARE PUBLISHED AS DELIBERATE FAILURES — do not read them as passing, and do not read the demotion as a verdict on the thesis. NKE (1.98:1) and LULU (1.97:1) are long_term longs against a 2.5 floor, and TLT's stop is 1.78 ATR against the 1.8 ETF floor. All three have FILLED entries that cannot be restated, and the only ways to make them pass are a target above anything the last year supports, a bear case above where a broken thesis would actually trade, or widening a winning short's stop after the fact. Each makes the trade worse to make a check pass, so the failing number is published instead. This is a construction lesson, not three coincidences: NKE, LULU and LCII are all long_term consumer names entered 10-12% above where they now trade with no stop and no bear case, and a long_term thesis published without a bear-case price cannot be risk-checked until it is already underwater. NO NUDGED RATIOS. Every win_probability exceeds its 1/(1+R:R) baseline, by 3.3 to 35.0 points; two deserve challenge rather than acceptance. GLD's 0.36 against a 0.304 baseline is a deliberately thin 5.6-point edge on a directional read the row itself calls unresolved. recommendations.counter_argument: Sell-side sentiment is going the other way and that is the real bear case, not a technicality: bullish share 38.9%, down 2.8 points over four months, revisions deteriorating. The answer is that the disagreement is the trade. Analysts are extrapolating the cliff; three insiders with the actual pipeline data in front of them committed $2.96M of their own money at 25.46-26.34 in early August, against $135K of sales. The stock has since traded up to 28.67 rather than fading, so the tape has sided with the insiders, not the desk notes. Conviction stays at 4 because the row already refuses to chase — the 27.60 ideal entry is below spot and the action says accumulate into 26.30-27.00, where they actually bought — but a buyer paying 28.67 today is not getting the trade the insiders got.

evidence.detail: Three distinct insiders bought $2.96M open-market in August 2026 against only $135K of sells: CEO ALBERT BOURLA 38,000 sh @ 26.34 (2026-08-12), Mortimer J Buckley 37,632 sh @ 25.52 and RONALD E BLAYLOCK 39,231 sh @ 25.46 (both 2026-08-05). recommendations.key_risk: TWO RISKS, and the entry is one of them. (1) FILL RISK: the 87.00 entry is 2.4% BELOW Friday's close, so this may simply never fill — and a pullback entry on a long fills only when the trade first goes against you. It is used here because 87.51 is the 200-day SMA reclaimed on 2x volume, a level I can point at, and because a market entry genuinely does not clear the floor. (2) INSIDER SELLING, unresolved and the reason conviction is 4 rather than the 5 the evidence count supports: **nine insider sells totalling $358.97M over six months against zero open-market buys**. That is the single largest sell figure of any name screened today and it is not explained by the guidance raise. Do not size this above 3%. RED TEAM: conviction CONFIRMED at 4, not lowered. The $358.97M of insider selling was tested as a reason to cut further and rejected: the row has already taken the one-notch discount for it (evidence supports 5, it is published at 4), and cutting twice for one fact is double-counting. recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that the eight-session slide was informed selling, not noise, and the $359M of insider distribution is what it looks like from the inside. CVS's own release supports caution: it raised guidance "while maintaining a cautious view for the remainder of the year in light of continued elevated cost trends and the potential for macro headwinds" — medical cost trend is the thing that has repeatedly broken this business. The answer is not that the risk is absent but that it is priced: at 11.1x a guided $8.00, the market is already discounting the raise almost entirely, and the stop at 82.00 sits below the level at which the reversal thesis is simply wrong.
